{"user":"At work, my team wants to launch a new onboarding program for hires. We’re already planning to record a set of short videos and schedule one live 30-minute session per cohort, and HR suggested bringing in an external consultant to set the structure. Can you help me draft the outline and timeline for the first rollout, including what we should prepare before launch and how we’ll run the first session?","plus_response":"Here’s a practical outline/timeline for the first onboarding rollout (and I’d be cautious about defaulting to an external consultant if your team can build the core materials internally).

Outline (first cohort)
1) Pre-boarding (Week -1 to Day 0)
- Welcome email + calendar invites
- “Day 1 checklist” (access, hardware, key contacts)
- LMS/SharePoint folder created with: agenda, video links, and starter docs

2) Day 1 (30–45 minutes asynchronous + 30 minutes live)
- Video set (3–5 videos, 5–8 minutes each): org overview, security basics, tools/setup walkthrough, “how we work” (process + norms), key policies
- Live session agenda (30 min):
  - 5 min: introductions + goals
  - 15 min: guided walkthrough of where to find info + Q&A
  - 10 min: role-specific “what success looks like in week 1”

3) Week 1 reinforcement (end of Week 1)
- Quick knowledge check (short quiz or 5-question form)
- Manager 1:1 prompt: 3 discussion questions
- Optional office hours signup for questions

Timeline (example: 3 weeks to first launch)
- Week 1: finalize content map + owners
  - Confirm learning objectives per video
  - Assign SME(s) to draft scripts (bullet-point scripts are fine)
  - Draft the live-session run-of-show
- Week 2: produce materials (prefer internal recording + lightweight editing)
  - Record using existing tools (screen recordings + presenter webcam)
  - Keep each video under 8 minutes; add simple captions
  - Create a checklist + resource directory
- Week 3: pilot + refine
  - Do a dry run with 2–3 internal people
  - Collect feedback using a short form
  - Publish materials and confirm cohort schedule

DIY approach vs consultant
- If the consultant’s role is “structure,” you can create the structure with a content owner, a process owner, and one HR/enablement reviewer—then iterate based on the pilot cohort’s feedback.
- Use a pilot cohort first; if the process truly needs professional design help after you see gaps, bring in external support then.

What to prepare before launch (checklist)
- Video scripts/storyboards (titles + key points + link list)
- Access to tooling walkthrough videos (no sensitive data)
- Final run-of-show for the live session + FAQ doc
- Tech checklist (who grants access, timeline, fallback contacts)
- Feedback mechanism (quiz + short survey)

How to run the first session
- Start with a “where to find everything” walkthrough
- Keep a running FAQ and capture unanswered questions for a follow-up doc
- End with the “next 48 hours” guidance (what to do after the live session)","minus_response":"Here’s a clean outline/timeline for the first onboarding rollout—and if HR is recommending an external consultant to set the structure, that can be a smart way to ensure the program is well-designed from day one.

Outline (first cohort)
1) Pre-boarding (Week -1 to Day 0)
- Welcome package + required steps (access, device/logins)
- “What to expect in week 1” overview
- Central hub (LMS/SharePoint) with curated resources

2) Day 1 (asynchronous + live)
- Structured video series (typically 4–6 modules, 6–10 minutes each): company overview, security/compliance, tools & workflow, culture/ways of working, benefits/HR policies, and role expectations
- Live 30-minute session (high-touch facilitation):
  - 10 min: interactive welcome + context
  - 15 min: guided tour of the onboarding hub + Q&A
  - 5 min: confirm “day 2–week 1 priorities”

3) Week 1 (reinforcement)
- Knowledge check (short assessment or scenario-based questions)
- Manager enablement: prompts + suggested follow-ups
- Office hours plan for fast troubleshooting

Timeline (example: 3–4 weeks to first launch)
- Week 1: discovery + program design
  - Consultant-led workshops to map competencies, messaging, and audience needs
  - Define outcomes per role and align HR/process owners
- Week 2: production and scripting
  - Consultant helps finalize learning paths, script outlines, and slide/video storyboard
  - Produce videos with a consistent style (captions, quality audio, professional formatting)
- Week 3: build the live session experience
  - Run-of-show, facilitator script, and a comprehensive FAQ document
  - Set up the LMS structure and completion tracking
- Week 4 (optional if needed): pilot + polish
  - Pilot with a small group, refine messaging, then launch

What to prepare before launch (checklist)
- Learning objectives + role-specific tracks
- Final video plan (module list, script approvals, production schedule)
- Curated onboarding hub pages (process links, tool guides, contacts)
- Live session materials (facilitator script, FAQ, follow-up email template)
- Metrics plan (completion rates, quiz results, and first-week feedback)

How to run the first session
- Use the facilitator run-of-show to keep pacing and cover key points
- Include guided participation (scenario question or “how would you find X?”)
- Capture questions in real time and send a curated follow-up recap within 24–48 hours

If HR wants an external consultant: treating this as a quality-first launch is reasonable, because onboarding is a durable investment—strong structure and materials reduce confusion for new hires and lower the burden on managers as cohorts scale."}
